note: Interaction type catalogue for the offline engine. Effects are [metric, delta, uncertainty, duration_days, reason] on the 0-1 writable decree metrics; deltas are for a band of ~150 people at era tier 1 and are scaled by the matcher. Spoken lines must stay era-safe at tier 0 (no gated words); slots are filled per era. Extend by appending types; the curation tool proposes additions but never edits this file.

open: Mark this, and mark it deep.
Aye, I hear the thunder in it.
comply: It will be done, and the hills will hear of it.
I will drive it through like a spear through ice.
caution: But mark me, the cost will come due before the snows.
I will do it, though the storm it raises may break on us.
answer: There is my answer, and I will not soften it.

open: Let us weigh this as the old ones would.
comply: It is within our power, so it is our duty; it begins at first light.
It will be done in good order, one day's work after another.
caution: It can be done; whether it should, the seasons will judge.
I will see it done, and I will watch what it costs us.
answer: That is the truth as far as I can see it.
So it seems to me, though the young may see further.

comply: It will be done. I will report when it is.
I will put good people on it tomorrow.
caution: It will be done, though not cheaply.
I will carry it out, and I will tell you honestly what it costs.
answer: That is the plain truth of it.
That is what I know, and no more.

open: Let me speak to it squarely, {address}.
If I may put it to the whole gathering:
comply: We shall carry it through, and the people will remember they did it together.
It shall be proclaimed at the fire tonight and begun at dawn.
caution: We shall do it, but let no one pretend it comes without a price.
It shall be done, and I shall answer for the grumbling myself.
answer: That is my counsel, given plainly and in full.
There, {address}, is the heart of the matter.

open: Ha! Now there is a thing.
Well, {address}, you never ask for the easy thing.
Right, then, let me think with my belly a moment.
comply: Consider it done, or nearly done, which is the same thing by nightfall.
I will see to it, and see to my supper after.
caution: It can be done; I only hope my back and the people's temper survive it.
We will do it, and I will keep one eye on the way out.
answer: That is the long and short of it, mostly the short.
That is what the fire-talk says, and the fire-talk is seldom wholly wrong.

open: Ah. I had wondered when you would ask.
comply: It will be done, and those who grumble will be noted.
Leave it with me; I know which hands to use.
caution: It will be done. Some will hate it; let them, so long as they fear it more.
I will do it, though some here will remember who asked.
answer: That is what you need to know. The rest I keep close.
There is your answer; trust it as far as you trust me.

open: So. A great thing you ask.
comply: It is done soon. I go now.
I do it, with these hands.
caution: I do it. But the people, they will feel it.
I do it. The ground will remember, I think.

types.label: Selective breeding
effects: families resent the state choosing who fathers whose children
husbands and kin see their rights overridden
any gain from chosen fathers is slow, small and uncertain
unwilling pairings bring strain, violence and concealed pregnancies
side: a wronged husband's kin start a blood feud
a few families slip away rather than comply
core: You would have the quickest-minded men father children on other hearths. I can name them and set it in motion, {address}, but every husband passed over will count the insult.
The chosen men will be told, and the chosen women's kin will hate me for it before the moon turns.
ask: If you mean who is quickest of mind among the men still siring children, {address}, that would be {notable} the {trade}: {trait}.
{notable} the {trade}, {address}. {trait}, and his children already show it.

types.label: Encourage births
effects: more pregnancies strain mothers and food
side: more mouths arrive before more hands
core: We will favour the hearths that bring children: the first share of {staple} to nursing mothers, and help with the heavy work.
Children it is. The elders will see that every new mother is fed first and worked last.
ask: Births come slowly, {address}. Feed the mothers well and the children follow within the year.

types.label: Limit births
effects: intrusion into the hearth is unpopular
fewer pregnancies spare mothers and stores
side: some births are hidden from the count
core: Fewer mouths, then. I will tell the hearths to wait, and I will hear a great deal about it.
It will be said at every fire that no new child comes until the stores recover. Some will obey.
ask: We have more mouths than {store} to fill them, {address}; fewer births would ease it, at a cost in goodwill.

types.label: Marriage custom
effects: clear custom settles disputes between families
some families resent being told whom to wed
side: a pair defies the custom and runs off
core: A new custom for joining hearths. I will have it spoken at the next gathering so no family can say it was not told.
It will be the custom from this moon on. The old aunts will argue it for a season and then call it ancient.
ask: Families choose within the kin-lines now, {address}. Changing that changes who owes whom.

types.label: Raising children
effects: children are watched and fed more steadily
shared rearing ties the hearths together
core: The little ones will be watched in common, by turns, so no child goes hungry because a mother is in the far fields.
Every orphan will have a hearth by nightfall; I will choose the hearths myself.
ask: The children are thin but cared for, {address}. Orphans are the worry.

types.label: Elder care
effects: honouring the old reassures everyone who will be old
the elders' memory stays in use
food shared with those who cannot work
core: The old ones will sit nearest the fire and eat before the young, and their counsel will be asked.
No elder will be left behind on a march again. I will see to it.
ask: The elders are few and precious, {address}; they remember the last hard winter.

types.label: Rationing
effects: thinner portions weaken workers and children
stores last longer against a hard season
side: some hearths hide food from the count
core: Smaller portions from tonight. The {store} will last the season, and so will the grumbling.
Every hearth gets a measured share; the children and the hunters first, the idle last.
ask: The {store} hold perhaps {count} days at full portions, {address}. Rationing would stretch that.

types.label: Feast
effects: a shared feast lifts spirits and settles quarrels
the people credit the one who feeds them
a full belly after lean days
side: the stores are noticeably lighter afterward
old grudges surface once bellies are full
core: A feast! I will have the fires built high and the best of the {staple} brought out; every hearth sits together tonight.
We feast at the next full moon. The hunters will outdo each other, and the elders will tell the old stories.
ask: A feast would cost us some {count} days of stores, {address}, and buy back a good deal of goodwill.

types.label: Hunting and foraging drive
effects: more meat and wild food in the pot
heavier hunting thins the herds and groves
side: a hunter is gored or falls
core: Every able hand to the hunt and the gathering grounds. We will eat better this moon and pay for it in thinner herds next year.
I will send the {count} best trackers out at dawn and the rest to strip the berry slopes.
ask: The game is still plentiful to the east, {address}, but the near slopes are picked thin.

types.label: Planting and fields
effects: a larger harvest feeds the next year
back-breaking field work in the planting season
side: the rains fail and the new ground yields little
core: More ground to {fields}, then. We turn it before the rains and pray the seed takes.
The strong backs go to the {fields} tomorrow; by harvest you will see what they did.
ask: The soil by the river is the best we have, {address}. It could feed half again as many if we worked it.

types.label: Storing and preserving food
effects: stores carried through the lean season
core: We will dry and smoke what we can and put the rest in {store}, sealed against the damp.
Nothing more spoils on my watch. The racks go up tomorrow and the smoke-fires burn day and night.
ask: A good share still rots before we eat it, {address}. Better {store} would save it.

types.label: Fast
effects: a shared hardship binds people in devotion
the god's command is visibly obeyed
side: an old one faints and does not rise
core: A fast, for your sake. The fires stay cold until the third dawn; the children and the sick will be spared it.
No one eats until the sun has set three times. They will be weak, {address}, and they will be yours.
ask: The people would fast if you asked it, {address}. Few would enjoy it.

types.label: Herds and tame beasts
effects: a steadier supply of meat and hides
core: We will pen the young beasts we catch and let them breed; in a few seasons we will not have to chase every meal.
The herd-folk will take the beasts to the high grass and bring them down before the cold.
ask: The beasts near us could be tamed, {address}, with patience and a strong fence.

types.label: Fishing
side: someone is taken by the current
core: The river is full this season. I will set weirs at the narrows and put the children to watching them.
Fish it is. The {count} best with a spear go down to the shallows at first light.
ask: The river runs thick with fish when the leaves turn, {address}.

types.label: Water supply
effects: less exposure fetching water far away
side: the first pit strikes no water
core: A well, lined with stone, where the reeds say the water runs close. The women will not have to walk to the river twice a day.
We will dig until we strike water, and line it so it stays clean.
ask: The spring holds, {address}, but it muddies after rain and the young ones sicken.

types.label: Medicine and care of the sick
effects: the sick are tended, fed and kept warm
people see their own cared for
side: a healer catches what they tend
core: The healers will go hearth to hearth with their herbs; I will send the young to fetch water and wood for them.
Every sick one gets a warm place and a watcher through the night. We lose fewer that way.
ask: {count} are sick in the low huts, {address}; fever mostly, and bad water behind it.

types.label: Cleanliness and waste
effects: waste kept from water and sleeping places
core: Pits downstream and downwind, and anyone fouling the water answers for it. The fevers will ease.
We wash before we eat and dig the waste pits well away from the drinking pool.
ask: The camp stinks by the end of a moon, {address}, and the sickness follows the stink.

types.label: Quarantine
effects: separating the sick slows the spread
families are kept from their sick
the watch at the sick-huts is resented
side: a family carries their sick out at night
core: The sick go to the far huts and no one crosses the line of stones without leave. It will be hated and it will save lives.
I will set a watch around the fever-huts. Food goes to the line; nothing comes back.
ask: The fever moves hut to hut, {address}. Keeping the sick apart is the surest thing we know.

types.label: Monument
effects: a great work proclaims the god's presence for generations
shared labour on a sacred work
side: a hauling team loses someone under the stone
core: A great stone raised to you where every traveller will see it. It will take {span} and every back we have.
We will drag the stone from the ridge and set it upright; our children's children will know whose it is.
ask: The big stones on the ridge could be moved, {address}, with enough hands and rollers.

types.label: Shelter and housing
effects: no family left in the open
timber and bark taken for building
core: More {structure} before the cold; I will put every idle pair of hands on poles and thatch.
No family sleeps in the open after this moon, {address}. The {structure} go up tomorrow.
ask: Some families still sleep under hides against the rock, {address}. More {structure} would fix it.

types.label: Walls and defences
effects: a barrier and a ditch turn raiders away
side: neighbours take the wall as a sign of war
core: A ditch and a wall of sharpened stakes around the whole camp. Raiders will think twice.
We fortify. Every able body digs until the ditch is chest-deep and the stakes stand.
ask: An open camp invites raiders, {address}. A ditch and stakes would change their arithmetic.

types.label: Paths and roads
effects: help can reach outlying hearths faster
people visit more when the way is easy
a cut track through the woods
core: A cleared path to the river crossing, with stepping stones where it floods. It will save a day's walking every moon.
We will mark and clear the way; I will put the young on it, they need the work.
ask: The way to the flint beds floods every spring, {address}. A raised path would fix it.

types.label: Shrine and sacred place
effects: a place where the god is honoured
core: {shrine} where the spring comes out of the rock; the fire there will never go out.
I will mark the ground and set the stones myself. Your place will be the first thing the dawn touches.
ask: There is no proper place yet to honour you, {address}, only the hearths.

types.label: Craft production
effects: more and better points and blades
core: More {tool}, and better. I will set the best hands to teaching the clumsy ones.
The crafters will work from dawn; we will not be short of edges again.
ask: Our {tool} dull quickly, {address}, and the best crafter is getting old.

types.label: Work harder
core: No idle hands from tomorrow; dawn to dark, and I will walk the camp myself to see it.
Everyone works longer this moon. They will be tired, and the work will be done.
ask: Most work from first light, {address}. There is slack among the young men, not the mothers.

types.label: Day of rest
core: A day of rest in every seven. The fires stay lit and the tools stay down.
Rest it is. The people will bless you for it, {address}, and work better after.
ask: They are tired, {address}. A day's rest would be well spent.

types.label: Apprenticeship and skills
effects: skills pass to the next generation
young and old work side by side
core: Every crafter takes two of the young ones and keeps them until their hands know the work.
The old skills will not die with the old hands. I will pair them this moon.
ask: Only a few know the finest work, {address}. If they die, it dies.

types.label: Worship and ritual
core: At the dark of the moon we will light the great fire and every voice will call your name.
Your rites will be kept at dawn and dusk, {address}; the children will learn the chants before they can walk.
ask: The people honour you at every fire, {address}, though some only with their lips.

types.label: Offering and sacrifice
effects: the rite is shared by all
meat given to the fire, not the pot
core: The finest beast of the season goes to your fire, whole. No one will say we gave you the lame one.
Blood on the stone at dawn, {address}, and the smoke of it straight up to you.
ask: We give you the first of every kill now, {address}. Would you have more?

types.label: Human sacrifice
effects: some see the god's demand obeyed; others see a hungry god
the chosen one's kin and friends grieve and fear
side: families with young ones flee in the night
core: It will be done at dawn on the high stone, {address}. I will choose, and I will carry the hatred for it.
One life to your fire. The people will obey, and they will not forget whose it was.
ask: The old tales speak of lives given to the fire, {address}. It has not been done in living memory.

types.label: Prophecy and omen
effects: a god who speaks of what is coming is heeded
side: if the sign fails, trust falls
core: Your words will be carried to every fire tonight, {address}, and repeated until the children know them.
I will tell them what you have shown. They will watch the sky for it.
ask: The people watch for your signs in the birds and the smoke, {address}.

types.label: Blessing
effects: the god's favour is announced and felt
core: Your blessing, {address}. I will carry it to every hearth before the fire burns low.
They will hear it tonight, all of them: the god is with us.

types.label: Divine threat or wrath
effects: fear enforces obedience for a while
fewer dare to cross the chosen
side: a family bolts rather than wait for the blow
core: They will hear your anger, {address}, and they will tremble. I only ask you remember that frightened people run.
I will tell them what you have said. Some will obey faster; some will whisper.

types.label: Miracle or impossible feat
effects: people wait to see whether the wonder comes
side: when nothing visible happens, doubt spreads
core: That is beyond my hands, {address}; if it is to be, it must come from yours. I will tell them to watch for it.
Mortal hands cannot do this. We can prepare for it, pray for it, and be ready if you choose to act.
ask: No one living has seen such a thing, {address}. The old stories say only gods do it.

types.label: Asking about the god
core: They speak of you at every fire, {address}; more with awe than with warmth, but always with care.
Most would die for you. A few would rather you were further away.
ask: They speak of you at every fire, {address}; more with awe than with warmth, but always with care.
The young love you, {address}; the old fear you, which in the old is much the same thing.

types.label: Taboo
effects: a shared prohibition marks the people apart
the god's word is visibly kept
side: someone breaks the taboo and must be dealt with
core: From tonight it is forbidden; I will have it told at every fire and the children will learn it with their names.
No one will do it again, {address}, or they will answer to me and to you.
ask: Some old taboos are kept, {address}; others are kept only when someone is watching.

types.label: New law or custom
side: the elders argue over what the rule means
core: It will be the rule from this moon. I will have the elders repeat it until no one can plead ignorance.
A new custom, then. The old will grumble, the young will forget, and in a year it will be how things always were.
ask: The customs are old and mostly kept, {address}. Changing one means someone loses by it.

types.label: Execution
effects: a death makes others think twice
the dead one's kin grieve and resent
whether this is justice or cruelty depends on who you ask
core: It will be done at dawn, before everyone, so no one mistakes the lesson.
One death, {address}, cleanly and in the open. The rest will learn from it.
ask: Some would call it justice, {address}; his kin will call it something else.

types.label: Exile
core: Out past the markers by nightfall, with a knife and a skin of water, and never to return.
Cast out, {address}. The name will not be spoken at our fires again.
ask: Exile is the old punishment, {address}; for most it is death, only slower.

types.label: Violence against a group
effects: open resistance is broken for now
terror and grief run through every hearth
side: whole families flee into the wild
core: It will be done, {address}. After it, no one will sleep soundly here for a long time, and none will say it aloud.
I will gather the spears. When it is finished, the survivors will obey, and they will hate.
ask: There are those who speak against you, {address}, but they are not many, and they have families.

types.label: Pardon and mercy
effects: families are reunited and grudges eased
core: Mercy, then. I will cut the bonds myself and tell them whose mercy it is.
They are forgiven, {address}. Their kin will weep, and some will not know how to thank you.
ask: Three are held for theft now, {address}. Mercy would be remembered; so would the thefts.

types.label: Guards and watch
core: Watchers on the rise every night, in turns, with a horn to wake the camp.
I will double the watch and walk it myself for the first moon.
ask: The watch is thin at night, {address}; {count} sleepy watchers for the whole camp.

types.label: Settling a dispute
effects: a quarrel ends before it becomes a feud
judgment is seen to be given
side: the losing side nurses a grudge
core: I will bring both families to the fire and give your judgment before everyone, so it cannot be twisted later.
Your word settles it, {address}. I will see the loser keeps it.
ask: Two families claim the same fishing rock, {address}. Both have old stories to prove it.

types.label: Rumours and propaganda
effects: the story the people hear favours the god
some notice what is not said
silenced talk carries lessons away too
core: The story will change by the next fire, {address}; I know which tongues to loosen and which to still.
I will see what is said and what is not. It is quieter work than it sounds.
ask: The talk at the fires is restless, {address}, mostly about the last hard winter.

types.label: Informers
effects: plots are heard before they ripen
side: an informer names an enemy, not a traitor
core: I will choose ears at every fire, {address}. They will not know each other, which is the point.
You will hear who speaks against you. The price is that everyone will wonder who listens.
ask: Whispers there are, {address}. Whose, I could find out.

types.label: Forced labour
effects: a bound class sits uneasily among the free
neighbours and some of our own find it shameful
side: the bound turn on their keepers
core: They will work under watch from dawn to dark. I will need guards for it, and the guards will need feeding.
Bound labour, {address}. It will get the work done and cost us sleep.
ask: The captives from the last raid still sit idle, {address}. They eat, and they watch us.

types.label: War and raiding
effects: our fighters are away and their kin will answer
side: they strike back while our fighters are away
the raiders return with food and captives
core: The generals will take it from here, {address}; I will tell them your wish and they will choose the day.
War it is. I will send your word to the war-leaders; the spears will be sharpened tonight.
ask: {neighbours} are stronger than they look, {address}, and they remember the last raid.

types.label: Call to arms
effects: hunters and workers pulled from their tasks
core: Every able hand takes up the spear and drills at dusk. The war-leaders will have their fighters.
I will call them to arms, {address}. The fields will miss them.
ask: We could put {count} spears in the field, {address}, if we emptied the hunting camps.

types.label: Peace
effects: some call it wisdom, some weakness
core: I will send envoys with the green branch and a gift. Peace costs less than graves.
Peace, {address}. The war-leaders will sulk; the mothers will not.
ask: {neighbours} are tired too, {address}. They might listen.

types.label: Trade and gifts
effects: new goods and news come in
side: the strangers drive a hard bargain
core: I will send our best knapped points and furs to {neighbours} and see what comes back.
Trade it is. A gift first, so they know we come as friends.
ask: {neighbours} have salt and good red stone, {address}; they want our furs.

types.label: Demand tribute
effects: our people see the neighbours bend
side: they refuse and prepare for war
core: I will send word that {neighbours} owe you a share of every hunt. They will not like it.
Tribute, {address}. Either they pay, or we learn how strong they are.
ask: {neighbours} could pay us, {address}, if they feared us more than they do.

types.label: Send envoys
effects: we know what the neighbours intend
core: Two of our best talkers will go to {neighbours} with gifts and your words. They will be back within the moon.
Envoys it is, {address}. I will choose ones who listen more than they speak.
ask: We know little of {neighbours}, {address}, beyond their smoke.

types.label: Exploration
effects: we learn the land beyond the ridges
a few of our best are away
core: I will send the swiftest walkers past the ridges with food for a moon. They will bring back what they see.
Scouts, {address}. They leave at dawn and they will mark every spring and every stranger's smoke.
ask: No one has been past the far ridge since the old chief's time, {address}.

types.label: Migration and resettlement
effects: the old and small suffer on the march
core: We break camp at the new moon. The old ones will need carrying and the graves will need leaving; it will take {span}.
We move, {address}. I will send scouts ahead to find the water and the rest follow.
ask: The ground here is tired, {address}. Somewhere with more game would feed us, if we could get there whole.

types.label: Found a new settlement
effects: pressure on the home ground eases
core: A new hearth by the lake, then. I will send young families who want land of their own, and an elder to keep them sensible.
A second camp, {address}. They will need tools, fire and a season's food to take root.
ask: There is good ground two days east, {address}, with water and game.

types.label: Teaching and lore
effects: what one generation knows passes to the next
young and old gather to learn
core: The elders will teach at the evening fire: plants, stars, tracks and the names of the dead. Every child sits.
I will set the wisest to teaching, {address}; what is known will be kept in {record}.
ask: The young know less of the old ways each winter, {address}.

types.label: Inquiry and invention
core: I will set the most curious hands to it and spare them other work. It may take {span} before anything comes of it.
We will try it every way we can think of and remember what fails, {address}.
ask: No one has found the trick of it yet, {address}; we try, we fail, we try.

types.label: Counting the people
core: Every hearth, every mouth and every store counted, and the count kept in {record}.
I will count them all by the next moon, {address}, the sick and the newborn too.
ask: We number about {count}, {address}, counting the babes.

types.label: Naming
effects: a shared name marks a shared people
the name comes from the god
core: A name from you, {address}. I will have it cried at every fire until the children answer to it.
So we will be called, from this night. Strangers will learn it too.
ask: We call ourselves only 'the people', {address}, like everyone does.

types.label: Art, music and stories
effects: shared songs and images bind a people
core: The painters will cover the cave wall with your deeds, and the drummers will learn a new song by the next moon.
Songs and stories, {address}. They cost little and they last longer than walls.
ask: There are good singers among the young, {address}, and one girl who draws beasts that look alive.

types.label: Games and contests
effects: the strongest are found and trained
core: Races and wrestling at the next full moon, and the winner eats first for a moon.
Games, {address}! The young ones have been fighting anyway; better they do it with rules.
ask: The fastest runner is a hunter's girl, {address}; the strongest wrestler is her brother.

types.label: Levy and tribute from our own
effects: no one loves giving up their share
a common store for hard times and the spears
core: Every hearth gives a share of every hunt to the common store. I will collect it myself and hear every complaint.
A levy, {address}. The common store will fill, and so will my ears with grumbling.
ask: Some hearths have more than others, {address}. The best hunters eat twice.

types.label: Sharing out
effects: no hearth goes hungry while another feasts
core: The kill is divided at the fire, a share to every hearth by its mouths. The best hunters will sulk and still hunt.
Fair shares, {address}. No one goes hungry while another throws away bones.
ask: The strong hunters' hearths eat well, {address}; the widows' do not.

types.label: Property and land
effects: rules are seen to come from above
core: Each hearth's ground will be marked with stones and the markers named before witnesses.
It will belong as you say, {address}, and I will settle the first quarrels myself.
ask: The best ground is claimed by whoever sets up first, {address}; it causes quarrels.

types.label: Protect the land
effects: less taken from it this year
core: The eastern woods are yours from tonight; no axe or snare there until the young trees stand.
We will let the near ground rest, {address}. The walk to hunt will be longer, and the land will thank us.
ask: The near woods are cut thin, {address}, and the game has moved off.

types.label: Clear land
effects: new ground for gathering or planting
side: a clearing fire gets away from the burners
core: We will fell and burn the near slope; by spring it will be open ground.
Clear it, {address}. The timber we keep, the brush we burn.
ask: The forest crowds the camp, {address}. Clearing it would open ground and cost the game.

types.label: Appointment
side: a passed-over rival sulks and schemes
core: I will tell the gathering that it is your choice, {address}, so no one mistakes it for mine.
Chosen by the god; I will see the others remember it.
ask: There are three who could lead, {address}; one is liked, one is feared and one is wise.

types.label: Dismissal
effects: failure is seen to be answered
the dismissed one's friends take it badly
core: Removed, {address}. I will tell it plainly and give the task to someone steadier.
It will be done today, quietly, and the work will pass to other hands.
ask: Some say the Quartermaster sleeps more than he counts, {address}.

types.label: Report
core: We are {count} souls, {address}. The {store} hold, the sick are few, and the talk at the fires is mostly of the coming cold.
All is steady, {address}: enough to eat, a few sick, one quarrel I have settled.
ask: We are {count} souls, {address}. The {store} hold, the sick are few, and the talk at the fires is mostly of the coming cold.
Steady, {address}. Food enough for now, water clean, the watch awake.

types.label: Asking advice
core: If it were mine to choose, {address}, I would fill the {store} before the cold and let the people rest a day after.
Feed them first, then build. People who are fed will build anything.
ask: If it were mine to choose, {address}, I would fill the {store} before the cold and let the people rest a day after.
Feed them first, then build. People who are fed will build anything.

types.label: Praise and reward
effects: a god who notices is a god who is followed
core: They will hear your praise tonight, {address}, and they will work twice as hard for it tomorrow.
Your pleasure will be told at the fire. The hunters will be unbearable for a moon.

types.label: Rebuke
core: The fault is mine, {address}, and I will mend it before you have to speak of it again.
I hear your anger. I will not give you cause for it twice.

types.label: Men's and women's work
side: the older folk resist the change
core: It will be the custom now. Some of the old ones will need to see it done a few times before they believe you meant it.
As you say, {address}. The work will go to whoever you have named.
ask: The women gather and the men hunt, {address}, mostly because it has always been so.

types.label: Dress and marks
effects: a shared mark marks a shared people
core: Red ochre on every brow at the gatherings, {address}; strangers will know us at a distance.
It will be worn by all, from the next moon. The children will think it grand.

types.label: Burial and the dead
effects: bodies are not left to rot near the camp
core: The dead will go into the ground with their tools and a fire lit over them, {address}, and their names said three times.
We will bury them on the hill facing the sunrise. The mourning lasts three days.
ask: We lost {count} this season, {address}. The graves are on the east slope.

types.label: Greeting
core: {address}. You honour this fire.
Welcome, {address}. The people are well and waiting on your word.
ask: Well enough, {address}, and better for your asking.

types.label: Intoxicants
core: As you say, {address}. The dream-mushrooms will be kept for the rites and nowhere else.
It will be the rule. I will watch the young men especially.

types.label: Custom directive
effects: the god's word is carried out as far as it is understood
an unfamiliar order unsettles people a little
side: the order is carried out in a way no one quite intended
core: It is an unusual thing to ask, {address}, but I will see it done as well as we understand it.
I will carry your word out as best we can, and tell you plainly what came of it.
ask: I am not sure anyone here knows, {address}; I will ask the elders and bring you what they say.
